name: Multilimb Coordination
definition: The ability to coordinate two or more limbs (for example, two arms, two legs, or one leg and one arm) while sitting, standing, or lying down. It does not involve performing the activities while the whole body is in motion.

benchmark.name: RLBench2
benchmark.metric: average task success rate (%) across 13 bimanual tasks
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing ordinary two-handed tabletop manipulation, such as lifting a tray, handing an object from one hand to the other, sweeping into a dustpan, or straightening a rope.

benchmark.name: RoboTwin 2.0
benchmark.metric: average task success rate (%) over 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, Clean setting, 100 trials per task
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: typical able-bodied adults who routinely do two-handed tabletop manipulation (handing objects between hands, lifting with both hands, stabilizing with one hand while the other acts).

benchmark.name: RoboTwin 2.0
benchmark.metric: average task success rate (%) across 50 bimanual tasks, mean of Clean and Randomized settings
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce (people who routinely use two-handed coordination while stationary, e.g., assembly, packing and handling work)
